ig_carousel_topic.topic: The Kelly criterion, explained without the math degree
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
How much should you actually bet?
Kelly has an answer.
Most bettors ignore it.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
The common mistake: flat-betting everything the same size regardless of edge.
A 3% edge and a 12% edge are not the same bet.
Sizing them identically throws away value or blows up your bankroll.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text:
Kelly sizes your bet based on two things: your edge and the odds.
Bigger edge, larger stake. Thinner edge, smaller stake.
The formula punishes both overbetting and underbetting.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
Example: You find a bet with a 56% win probability at -110 odds (1.909 decimal).
Full Kelly says stake 6.4% of your bankroll.
Most serious bettors use half-Kelly (3.2%) to reduce variance without killing expected growth.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text:
You don't need to run the formula every pick.
But understanding it changes how you think about bet sizing.
Edge without discipline is just noise.
ig_carousel_topic.caption: Kelly criterion, sized down to what actually matters. Understand this and you'll think about every bet differently.
